# Summary

Full code can be found [here]().

## Data

All election data comes from [ElectionData.MY](https://electiondata.my){target="_blank"},
the public face of the Malaysian Election Corpus (MECo;
[Scientific Data, 2025](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41597-025-06502-7){target="_blank"}).
The site dedicates its data to the public domain (CC0). I ran the query on the site's own
[Query Builder](https://electiondata.my/query-builder/){target="_blank"}; the SQL for each export is in `queries/` and the exports are
in `data/raw/`. 

### Step 1: Lorem ipsum

Lorem ipsum

::: {.callout-note collapse="false" appearance="minimal" title="Show query"}
```sql
-- 01_turnout_context.sql
-- Purpose: average Johor DUN turnout, SE-13 to SE-16 (context plot)
-- Note: unweighted mean of seat turnouts, not state turnout
SELECT
  election, date, COUNT(*) AS n_seats, ROUND(AVG(voter_turnout), 1) AS avg_turnout
FROM
  headline_stats
WHERE
  state = 'Johor'
  AND election IN ('SE-13', 'SE-14', 'SE-15', 'SE-16')
GROUP BY
  election, date
ORDER BY
  date
```
:::




### Step 2: Do the same 56 seats appear in SE-15 and SE-16?

Run in the electiondata.my Query Builder. Zero rows means every seat name matches.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal" title="Show query"}
```sql
-- 02_seat_names.sql
-- Purpose: list Johor seats present in only one of SE-15 and SE-16.
SELECT a.seat AS seat_se15, b.seat AS seat_se16
FROM (SELECT seat FROM headline_stats
      WHERE state = 'Johor' AND election = 'SE-15') a
FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT seat FROM headline_stats
                 WHERE state = 'Johor' AND election = 'SE-16') b
  ON a.seat = b.seat
WHERE a.seat IS NULL OR b.seat IS NULL
```
:::
